title: Stop logging inside signal handlers
hook: Why are signal handlers so dangerous, and what is `signalfd` or `sigaction` safety?

scenes.caption: A handler can interrupt code while its internal state is inconsistent.
scenes.narration: A service hangs during shutdown after logging inside its signal handler. The handler may have interrupted library code; calling printf or malloc there is unsafe.

items: sigaction does not make calls safe

scenes.caption: Keep the handler minimal and perform cleanup in normal control flow.
scenes.narration: For a simple single threaded loop, install a handler with sigaction that only sets a volatile signal atomic flag. The main loop handles cleanup.

items: A flag alone will not wake blocked I/O

scenes.caption: Linux signalfd moves signal handling into an ordinary read loop.
scenes.narration: Alternatively, block the chosen signals before creating threads and read them from signalfd. Handle termination in the event loop, where ordinary cleanup is allowed.

items: Block these signals in every thread
Watch the descriptor with poll or epoll

scenes.caption: Signal delivery is not the same thing as a completed shutdown.
scenes.narration: Send termination while the service is busy and watch it exit. Check interrupted system calls deliberately; restart behavior depends on the call and handler flags.

elements.text:
kill -TERM "$pid"
# In the event loop:
# read signal → stop accepting work
# drain bounded work → exit

takeaway: Use a minimal sigaction handler, or block signals and consume them through signalfd in normal code.
